- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.06) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.22) and price is falling, model often overcorrects downward; avoid sharp drops; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to prevent overreaction.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +0.5–1.5% bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to lag; use 1–2 day smoothing or add 0.3–0.7% lag correction to forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizon; if model is above 1.5σ from recent mean, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 5 days.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.05 for 3+ days), model often underestimates; add 0.2–0.8% upward bias to avoid “flat” underprediction.
